note: Section 1: real llama.cpp/ggml backend architecture study, done by reading the pinned submodule source (third_party/llama.cpp, commit c0bc8591e8815c63cb01dd3f051a8b0df02501c9, the same commit every prior MEMBRANE phase has used) before writing any new code. Every claim below cites a real file/line from that source tree, read directly in this session.

q1_can_copy_kv_tensor_cpu_vulkan_via_pub.evidence: ggml_backend_tensor_copy (ggml/src/ggml-backend.cpp:477-498) dispatches on ggml_backend_buffer_is_host() for src/dst: host->device uses ggml_backend_tensor_set, device->host uses ggml_backend_tensor_get, and even device-to-device-of-different-backend falls back to a host-staged malloc/get/set round trip if no direct backend_buffer_copy_tensor path exists. This is a fully public, already-used-elsewhere API (ggml-backend.h:71,92,93) -- confirmed genuinely cross-backend, not CPU-only.

q2_can_tensor_backing_buffer_be_rebound_.evidence: No public API sets tensor->buffer on an already-initialized tensor to a DIFFERENT already-allocated buffer. ggml_backend_tensor_alloc(buffer, tensor, addr) (ggml-backend.h:426) only initializes a tensor's data pointer into a buffer at allocation time, and llama-kv-cache.cpp only ever calls this path implicitly via ggml_backend_alloc_ctx_tensors_from_buft during construction (llama-kv-cache.cpp:284-301), never again afterward. There is no llama_kv_cache public method to move an existing k/v tensor to a new buffer in place.

q3_can_paired_cpu_gpu_tensors_be_maintai.evidence: Because the compute graph is rebuilt fresh on every decode call (llama-context.cpp:1352, model.build_graph(gparams), called from the per-decode process path, not cached across calls), a graph built AFTER a caller swaps which raw ggml_tensor* a kv_cache layer's k/v slot points to will naturally reference the new tensor and its (new) backend. This makes a caller-managed pair of tensors (one CPU-backed, one GPU-backed, kept content-identical via ggml_backend_tensor_copy) a workable logical-swap unit BETWEEN decode calls -- but only if the caller can actually substitute the pointer llama_kv_cache itself uses (see limitation below).

q4_does_compute_graph_assume_kv_tensors_.answer: only for the duration of a single graph build+compute, not for the whole context lifetime
q4_does_compute_graph_assume_kv_tensors_.evidence: llama-context.cpp:1352 shows the graph is a fresh ggml_cgraph built from the model/kv-cache's CURRENT tensor pointers on every call -- nothing in the graph itself is backend-pinned across decode calls; the pinning is really just 'each individual kv_layer struct instance points to exactly one ggml_tensor, and that tensor lives in exactly one buffer for its whole existence.'

q5_is_backend_placement_determined_once_.answer: at KV-cache-object construction time (llama_kv_cache::llama_kv_cache), which happens once per llama_context, not once per graph -- a NEW kv_cache object could in principle place layers differently, but the ALREADY-LIVE kv_cache's tensors are placed exactly once, at that object's construction, via ggml_backend_alloc_ctx_tensors_from_buft (llama-kv-cache.cpp:284-301)
q5_is_backend_placement_determined_once_.evidence: llama-kv-cache.cpp:214-225: per-layer buft is resolved from model.dev_layer(il) (the SAME per-layer device assignment used for weight offload, i.e. n_gpu_layers) when offload=true, else forced to ggml_backend_cpu_buffer_type(). This is resolved ONCE per layer, in the constructor, not re-resolved per graph build.

q6_is_a_public_api_only_tiering_path_pos.answer: yes for STATIC, load-time, per-layer GPU/CPU placement of WEIGHTS+KV TOGETHER (already exists, unmodified, via --gpu-layers N partial offload -- but see critical_correction_weight_kv_coupling below: this is NOT KV-specific); yes for coarse DYNAMIC movement via public llama_state_seq_get_data/set_data transfer between two differently-configured contexts sharing one loaded model; NO for true in-place, single-layer-independent VRAM release/rebind within one already-live context, because of the shared-buffer allocation limitation below; NO for KV-only placement independent of weight placement, for the reason in critical_correction_weight_kv_coupling.
q6_is_a_public_api_only_tiering_path_pos.shared_buffer_limitation: ggml_backend_alloc_ctx_tensors_from_buft (ggml/src/ggml-alloc.c:1167-1244, confirmed by direct read) packs ALL same-buft tensors in a ggml_context into one (or a small number of, only split when a per-buffer max_size cap is hit) shared ggml_backend_buffer. llama-kv-cache.cpp groups ALL GPU-offloaded layers' k/v tensors into ONE ggml_context per buft (ctx_for_buft, llama-kv-cache.cpp:104-127), so in the common case every GPU-resident layer's KV lives in ONE shared Vulkan buffer. ggml_backend_buffer_free frees an entire buffer at once -- there is no public partial-free/defragment API. Freeing ONE demoted layer's VRAM while N-1 other GPU-resident layers' KV stays allocated is therefore NOT possible without either (a) tearing down and reallocating the WHOLE shared buffer (which means copying every still-resident layer's data out and back in too, not just the demoted one), or (b) llama.cpp allocating one buffer PER TENSOR instead of per buft-group, which is not exposed as a caller-selectable option anywhere in llama_context_params/llama_model_params.

classification: E. REQUIRES_LLAMA_CPP_CHANGE (for the phase's actual target capability -- KV-cache placement decoupled from weight placement); a real but COARSER mechanism (C-adjacent: copy possible, and a combined weight+KV placement win IS possible) already exists for a different, related capability -- see both findings below, neither alone is the whole story.

critical_correction_weight_kv_coupling.finding: model.dev_layer(il) -- the per-layer device lookup llama-kv-cache.cpp:214-225 uses to place EACH LAYER's KV buft -- is the EXACT SAME per-layer device assignment llama-model.cpp uses to place that layer's WEIGHTS (llama-model.cpp:1307: i_gpu_start = max(n_layer_all + 1 - n_gpu_layers, 0); layers before i_gpu_start are forced CPU for BOTH weights and KV). This was verified directly against real gpu_policy.estimated_model_bytes numbers in this phase's own membrane-run output: at ctx=16384 on SmolLM2-135M, moving from --gpu-layers 30 (full) to --gpu-layers 15 (half) drops estimated_model_bytes from 212474880 to 106237440 bytes (~101 MiB less WEIGHT VRAM) in addition to the ~96 MiB less KV VRAM for the demoted layers -- the two effects sum almost exactly to the measured external VRAM delta (see memory_accounting.json). This means --gpu-layers N is NOT an independent KV-cache-placement mechanism -- it moves a layer's COMPUTE (weights) to CPU right along with its KV, which is a materially different, coarser thing than the phase's stated goal ('hot/recent KV -> GPU VRAM... with controlled movement/prefetch' implicitly assumes weights stay GPU-resident for fast compute, only the cache moves). No public llama_context_params/llama_model_params field lets a caller decouple KV buft resolution from model.dev_layer(il) for the standard (non-override) KV cache construction path.

smallest_change_that_would_fix_this.function: llama_kv_cache::llama_kv_cache constructor, the per-layer buft-resolution block (~lines 211-225)
smallest_change_that_would_fix_this.change: add an optional caller-supplied per-layer KV-device-override callback (ggml_backend_dev_t (*kv_dev_override)(int32_t il, void *ud)), consulted INSTEAD OF model.dev_layer(il) when non-null, exactly mirroring the shape of the ALREADY-EXISTING, ALREADY-INTEGRATED-INTO-THIS-REPO (not this phase's proposal -- a prior, separate, already-applied patch) kv_type_override callback (patches/llama.cpp-membrane-kv-type-override.patch) -- same precedent, same risk profile, same threading pattern through llama_context_params -> llama_memory_params -> llama_kv_cache constructor.
smallest_change_that_would_fix_this.generic_upstreamable_reasoning: this is a narrow, additive, backward-compatible extension point (NULL callback = identical to current upstream behavior) of exactly the same shape llama.cpp's own maintainers already accepted the pattern for (per-tensor type overrides are common in the ggml ecosystem; per-tensor/per-layer device overrides are a natural, minimal generalization, not a novel architectural concept)
smallest_change_that_would_fix_this.maintenance_risk: LOW -- same shape and same file the repo already successfully maintains a patch against (kv_type_override); the two patches would likely need to be kept in sync with each other on every llama.cpp submodule bump, which is a real but bounded, already-familiar cost (see docs/phase4-runtime-policy.md's existing process for the type-override patch).

static_placement_already_exists_but_coup.finding: llama.cpp's existing, upstream, unmodified --gpu-layers N (partial offload) mechanism gives MEMBRANE per-layer GPU-vs-CPU placement for BOTH weights and KV TOGETHER, because llama-kv-cache.cpp resolves each layer's KV buft via the SAME model.dev_layer(il) lookup used for weight offload (llama-kv-cache.cpp:214-225 -- see critical_correction_weight_kv_coupling above). A context created with e.g. --gpu-layers 16 on a 32-layer model places 16 layers' weights+K/V tensors in a real Vulkan buffer and the other 16 layers' weights+K/V tensors in a real CPU buffer -- genuinely reduced GPU bytes, not a shadow copy, with zero MEMBRANE code changes and zero llama.cpp changes required. This is a REAL, USABLE, TODAY mechanism (see vram_reduction.json/second_model.json/pressure_test.json), but it is not KV-specific tiering -- it is coarse combined offload that happens to include KV as a side effect. This was previously invisible to MEMBRANE's own research because every prior phase (Q8/Q5/mixed/adaptive) always requested --gpu-layers all.
static_placement_already_exists_but_coup.caveat: this is a STATIC split fixed at context-creation time by n_gpu_layers, and it moves LAYER COMPUTE to CPU (slower matmuls for those layers), not just cache storage -- it is not 'hot recent tokens on GPU', and it is not 'KV moves, weights stay put for fast compute.' It still answers Section 6 (tiering unit, at a coarser-than-intended granularity) and gives a genuinely real win for Section 9's VRAM-reduction test, but does not satisfy the phase's actual 'KV cache placement, controlled movement/prefetch, weights presumably staying resident' goal -- that requires the patch above.

async_transfer_findings_for_section_15.cpy_tensor_async_exists_in_public_api: yes -- ggml_backend_tensor_copy_async(backend_src, backend_dst, src, dst), ggml-backend.h:116, ggml-backend.cpp:500-518
async_transfer_findings_for_section_15.vulkan_backend_implements_it: yes -- ggml_backend_vk_cpy_tensor_async, ggml/src/ggml-vulkan/ggml-vulkan.cpp:15872, registered in the backend iface table at line 17262
real_conditions_observed_in_the_vulkan_i: device-to-device async copy only works within the SAME physical device (ggml-vulkan.cpp:15889-15892, returns false otherwise, caller then falls back to a blocking ggml_backend_tensor_copy)

host(CPU)-to-device async copy requires the HOST buffer to be Vulkan-pinned memory obtained via ggml_vk_host_get (ggml-vulkan.cpp:15903-15906) -- a plain malloc'd host buffer returns pinned_buf==nullptr and the function returns false, again falling back to a synchronous copy

when pinned and same-device, Vulkan does use a real dedicated transfer queue path when ctx->device->async_use_transfer_queue is set (ggml-vulkan.cpp:15911-15915), separate from the compute queue -- genuine hardware-level async transfer capability exists, not just an API stub
async_transfer_findings_for_section_15.implication: a naive MEMBRANE tiering implementation using plain malloc'd host buffers would silently fall back to synchronous copies every time (the async entry point returns false), even though real async hardware support exists underneath -- getting the real overlap benefit requires deliberately allocating pinned host memory via the same ggml_vk_host_get/backend host-buffer-type mechanism, not just calling the async API and hoping.

sliding_window_attention_note_for_sectio.finding: grep of the pinned llama.cpp source confirms hparams.swa_type / n_swa / llama_swa_type machinery exists and llama-kv-cache.h's own swa_type field (llama-kv-cache.h:263) is read at KV-cache-construction time, meaning SWA-aware models get a bounded/ring-buffer KV cache shape rather than a monotonically-growing one -- relevant to Section 17, checked in detail there against the two actual test models used in this phase.

conclusion_for_stop_condition_section_2.reasoning: no llama.cpp source was modified this phase (per Section 2's instruction to STOP and report, not patch). The probes this phase DID run (byte-level copy round-trip proof, live-context round-trip without buffer teardown, coarse combined weight+KV placement via existing --gpu-layers N) are all real and achievable with zero llama.cpp changes, and are reported in full. But the phase's actual target capability -- KV-cache placement decoupled from weight placement, with controlled live movement -- does genuinely require a llama.cpp change (see critical_correction_weight_kv_coupling.smallest_change_that_would_fix_this above); this phase identifies that change precisely, argues it is generic/upstreamable and low-risk (same shape as the already-accepted kv_type_override patch), and explicitly does NOT write it, per Section 2. Two named follow-up patches would be needed for a complete solution: (a) the KV-device-override callback described here, for weight/KV decoupling, and (b) the separate per-tensor-buffer-allocation change noted in the (still valid) shared-buffer discussion, for true single-layer-independent live VRAM release. Neither is written in this phase.
